sentences.text:
This writ petition has been filed for issuance of writ of mandamus, directing the respondents 1 to 3,
to act upon the revised valuation statement submitted by the fourth respondent on 16.03.2020 and consequently, to revise the compensation and pay additional compensation to the petitioner to the tune of Rs.68,24,200/- along with solatium with respect to the subject property that was acquired by the National Highways.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.

Heard Mr.R.Thangapandian, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms.S.Jeyapriya, learned Government Advocate for the respondents.
3. The case of the petitioner is that he was the absolute owner of the property measuring an extent of 2 acres 96 cents in S.No.1009/2 in Nadumandalam village, Natham Taluk, Dindigul District.
In this property, the petitioner had planted various trees and had also also dug four bore wells and laid drip irrigation.
The proceedings were initiated for acquisition of the land by the National Highways Department.
Accordingly, it was acquired and the compensation was also fixed.

The petitioner made objections and requested the second respondent to reconsider and enhance the compensation, since according to the petitioner, the loss incurred for the trees that were available in the property was not considered at the time of calculating the compensation.
4. On the request made by the petitioner, the second respondent instructed the sixth respondent to conduct an enquiry and to submit a report.
The sixth respondent, through letter dated 14.01.2020 instructed the fourth respondent to assess the value of the left out trees.
Accordingly, the fourth and fifth respondents inspected the property and submitted a revised assessment https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis report dated 30.01.2020.

The same was submitted to the sixth Raaviyathammal vs / on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47488736/
2 respondent through letter dated 04.02.2020 and as per the revised assessment report, the value of the trees was assessed at Rs.68,24,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The grievance of the petitioner is that inspite of the report submitted, the revised additional compensation has not been paid to the petitioner and left with no other option, the present writ petition has been filed before this Court.

5. The learned Government Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents submitted that the report submitted by the Horticulture Department has been taken into consideration by the second respondent and the second respondent will take a decision on the claim made by the petitioner on the additional compensation within the time frame stipulated by this Court.

The learned Government Advocate further submits that the report has already been received by the second respondent from the sixth respondent and hence, sometime is required for taking a final decision on the claim made by the petitioner.

6. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and the submission made by the learned Government Advocate, there shall be a direction to the second respondent to consider the report submitted by the fourth https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and sixth respondents and deal with the request made by the petitioner seeking for revised additional compensation and a final decision shall be taken within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
7. This writ petition is disposed with the above terms.
No costs.
